faq.q: How do I know what helps me?
faq.a: Notice when learning feels easier. Is it when it is quiet? When you see pictures? When you can move? That is a clue.
asks: Tell me about What helps me?

faq.q: When should I tell my teacher?
faq.a: Pick a calm moment, like before or after a lesson. Or write it on a note if talking feels hard.
asks: Tell me about A good moment

faq.q: What can I say to my teacher?
faq.a: Start with, It helps me when... For example, It helps me when you write the steps down, or It helps me to sit at the front.
asks: Tell me about She says it
Tell me about Steps written down

faq.q: What if I feel shy telling my teacher?
faq.a: You can write a note, or ask a grown-up you trust to come with you. You can also practise the words at home first.
Most teachers are glad. Knowing what helps you makes their job easier too.
asks: Tell me about Teacher is glad

facts: Speaking up for what you need is called self-advocacy.
Many schools make changes, like seating or extra time, to help children learn their way.

quiz.say: What is a good way to start telling your teacher?
quiz.why: It helps me when... is clear and kind, so your teacher knows how to help.

wrong.1: Blaming can upset your teacher. Say what helps.
wrong.2: Saying what helps works better than refusing.

quiz.say: When is a good time to talk to your teacher?

options.show: In the middle of a test
options.say: In the middle of a test

quiz.why: After the lesson, your teacher has time to listen.

wrong.1: In a test, your teacher cannot talk.
wrong.2: In a fire drill, everyone must listen and walk out.
